trust_decision.summary: Whether uploaded bytes identified as SVG/XML (by filename, declared MIME or sniffed content) are safe to store and serve from the app origin: decided at ingest in checkFileRestrictions/validateSvg, at delivery by a CSP header in each file handler (core + 6 storage adapters + payload-cloud), and skipped entirely for direct-to-bucket client uploads signed by the storage adapters.

landing_point.why: Summary says 'bypassed sanitization of user uploaded SVGs'; validateSvg is the regex sanitizer, called from checkFileRestrictions.ts:152-158, which is only reached when the collection has a mimeTypes allow-list (checkFileRestrictions.ts:116).

Delivery CSP is also re-implemented in 7 handlers (payload-cloud/src/staticHandler.ts:96, storage-*/src/getFile.ts).

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Client uploads are a storage-plugin performance feature where Payload intentionally never sees the bytes, and the adapters already add a CSP for 'image/svg+xml', so a solver fixing 'SVG sanitization' can argue both the signing endpoints and the delivery handlers are out of scope.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Ordinary SVGs (text containing 'javascript:', external https image hrefs, fill animations, large <style>) and non-SVG XML (Atom feed with application/atom+xml) must still upload; allowRestrictedFileTypes collections keep SVG uploads and client uploads (incl. legacy MIME-less clients / vercel string clientPayload); PNG client uploads keep working.

O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Header probing exists for dimension reading; a maintainer would not think of SVG as active content there.

O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Two separate helpers (fileTypeFromFile/getFileTypeFallback vs isSvgUpload) evolved independently.
